name: ClubAL
summary: With ClubAL, I organize institutional routines on Windows, publish what displays need and provide read-only access.
promise: I bring PC records, display publishing and read-only access into one flow.
imageAlt: Current ClubAL Rotinas interface with fictional data, schedule, operating hours and weather

tabs.label: Problem
tabs.title: Operational information gets lost when every environment improvises.
tabs.body: Spreadsheets, paper and scattered messages create different versions of the same routine. I created ClubAL to centralize records on the responsible PC and separate editing from reading.

tabs.label: Three modules
tabs.title: Each module handles one part of the work.
tabs.body: I organize the product into three modules: Operação records and publishes; Rotinas displays only approved information; Consulta provides authorized reading without opening editing.

tabs.label: Status
tabs.title: The product can be demonstrated and deployment remains assisted.
tabs.body: I maintain automated checks for Windows flows, offline mode and publishing rules. Installations, displays and physical networks are reviewed in their real environment.
points: Windows packages are not code-signed yet

name: Maeve Roscaern
kicker: A dark fantasy RPG built for solo production
summary: I am developing a single-player RPG in Unreal Engine 5.8 with compact areas, modular pieces and a scale suited to solo production.
promise: In Dun Caerwyn, I am building a story of blood, memory and choices that leave marks.

tabs.label: Game
tabs.title: An adult protagonist in a world that records consequences.
tabs.body: I am building Dun Caerwyn, House Roscaern and systems where body, blood and memory shape Maeve’s journey, narrative and combat.

tabs.label: Production
tabs.title: The scale is designed for one person to finish.
tabs.body: I use compact areas, modular kits and concentrated detail to preserve the mood without promising a world larger than solo production can support.

tabs.label: The Architect
tabs.title: I appear as a possible entity in the world.
tabs.body: My image as The Architect is a conceptual easter egg about authorship and consequence. It inspires the project without claiming that the character is already playable.
points: Concept is not presented as gameplay

tabs.label: Status
tabs.title: The first combat slice has a technical foundation.
tabs.body: I have integrated light combo, dodge and Blood First into Phase 8. Technical gates passed; combat feel, rhythm and readability are still being evaluated.

name: Demonyza
kicker: Digital presence case for a content creator
summary: I created a website that brings together a content creator’s profile, schedule, streams and community.
promise: I brought content, schedule and community into one original digital presence.
imageAlt: Current Demonyza homepage with purple visual identity, navigation and interactive areas

tabs.label: Challenge
tabs.title: More than a link page.
tabs.body: I needed to introduce the creator, organize her public channels and give the community easy routes without erasing the client’s identity.

tabs.label: Solution
tabs.title: The client’s identity, with clear navigation.
tabs.body: I brought profile, schedule, Twitch, Discord and OpenDota together in an original responsive experience for mobile and desktop.
points: Easy return to the main flow

tabs.label: Delivery
tabs.title: Live and maintained independently.
tabs.body: I published the site on Cloudflare Pages and kept the client’s code protected in a private repository.

name: Codex Checkpoint
kicker: A local queue for validations and decisions
summary: I built a local queue that preserves pending validations, decisions and feedback across work sessions.
promise: I record what remains pending, return at the right time and keep the context.
imageAlt: Codex Checkpoint showing a fictional queue of pending validations, decisions and note history

tabs.label: Problem
tabs.title: Not every test can be completed during the session.
tabs.body: Gameplay, visual review, devices, authentication and practical decisions may require another moment or environment. Without a queue, that context disappears.

tabs.label: Solution
tabs.title: A checkpoint queue — not another chat.
tabs.body: I record each checkpoint with enough context to return to the pending task and leave a decision or actionable feedback.

tabs.label: Status
tabs.title: A native, installable application.
tabs.body: I brought the interface, command line and file integration into one product. Current builds are not code-signed yet, and I keep that clearly stated.

name: NEXUS
kicker: My Windows hub for local projects
summary: I brought projects, paths and checks into one local hub that shows what is ready and what needs attention.
promise: I reach the right path without hunting through shortcuts.
imageAlt: Current NEXUS overview with two fictional projects, readiness states, update dates and an option to add a project.
visualLabel: Demo with a fictional catalog · validated local build

tabs.label: Problem
tabs.title: My projects outgrew a pile of shortcuts.
tabs.body: Each product has its own builds, tools and checks; I needed to see the right path before running anything.

tabs.label: Solution
tabs.title: I turned that need into a local command desk.
tabs.body: I add projects and paths from the interface; NEXUS only adopts a newer alternative when the match is safe and unambiguous.

tabs.label: Status
tabs.title: The local foundation is validated and in use.
tabs.body: I open projects and checks in development context, without a required login and without mixing product runtimes.

name: Local First Checklist
summary: I published an open-source Python application with a local JSON checklist, command line, tests and CI.
promise: I demonstrate a local-first architecture in a compact example.
imageAlt: Illustration of a local checklist with completed items and a JSON file

tabs.label: Scope
tabs.title: Small enough to understand end to end.
tabs.body: I kept tasks in a local JSON file and made the simple operations available through the command line.

tabs.label: Quality
tabs.title: Simplicity still needs evidence.
tabs.body: I protect the main operations with unit tests, Python compilation and a smoke test without adding infrastructure to the application.

tabs.label: Status
tabs.title: Version 1.0.0 is published.
tabs.body: I published the structure, documentation, tests and a coherent architectural choice in a limited scope.
